# Audit schema v1

Every audit record is an OTLP LogRecord with EventName `audit` and the
attributes below, and no others (the closed set). Go writers spell keys
through the generated `audit.Key*` constants and test their records with
`audit.Check` and `audittest`; other writers use `cmd/auditschema`.

## Writers

| writer | code | who |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | H | A request a component served for a caller, recorded by that component: snowplow for a person's or an agent's request, authn for a login and a /delegate token. |
| `gateway` | G | The agent gateway's hop record, projected by the collector. |
| `action` | T | An agent's per-action record, written by whatever performs the action. |
| `controller` | C | A controller reconcile. |

## Levels

- **R**: required. **R (mark)**: required, or omitted and named in
  `krateo.audit.incomplete` when the writer cannot establish it.
- **C: when**: required when *when* holds. **[checked]**: `Check` evaluates the
  condition on the record. Without it, the condition is not visible on the
  record and `Check` treats the key as optional, unless it is **(mark)**: then
  it must be present or marked.
- **O**: optional. **NE**: not established by this writer, never written.
  **—**: does not apply.

## The target rule

Every record names its target: `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource` (a Kubernetes object) or `server.address`
(an external endpoint). Marker `target`.

| writer | targets |
|---|---|
| `request` | exactly one |
| `gateway` | exactly one |
| `action` | exactly one |
| `controller` | at least one |

## Conditions `Check` evaluates

- `k8s_target`: The record names a Kubernetes object: k8s.namespace.name or any krateo.audit.object_ref.* key is present.
- `write`: krateo.audit.verb is a write: create, update, patch, delete, deletecollection (a Kubernetes object), post or put (anything else).
- `method_other`: http.request.method is _OTHER: the writer was given a method semconv does not name.
- `delegated`: The record carries a delegation: krateo.audit.delegation or krateo.audit.on_behalf_of.user.name is present.
- `impersonated`: The record carries an impersonation: either krateo.audit.impersonated_user.* key is present.
- `caused`: The record names the object a controller reconciled: any krateo.audit.cause_ref.* key is present.
- `denied`: krateo.audit.outcome is denied: the writer itself refused.

## Closed values per writer

A key whose values depend on the writer lists them per writer class. `Check`
reports any other value as `bad-enum`, and the key on a writer class that
declares none as `not-for-writer`. A writer gains a value in a minor
release, by adding it to `schema/v1.yaml`. Go writers spell each value
through its generated constant.

| key | value | writers | Go constant |
|---|---|---|---|
| `krateo.audit.denial_reason` | `name_reserved` | `request` | `audit.DenialReasonNameReserved` |
| `krateo.audit.denial_reason` | `name_claimed` | `request` | `audit.DenialReasonNameClaimed` |
| `krateo.audit.denial_reason` | `name_held_legacy` | `request` | `audit.DenialReasonNameHeldLegacy` |
| `krateo.audit.denial_reason` | `name_provisioned` | `request` | `audit.DenialReasonNameProvisioned` |
| `krateo.audit.denial_reason` | `name_bound` | `request` | `audit.DenialReasonNameBound` |
| `krateo.audit.denial_reason` | `system_group` | `request` | `audit.DenialReasonSystemGroup` |
| `krateo.audit.denial_reason` | `kept_resource_policy` | `controller` | `audit.DenialReasonKeptResourcePolicy` |

## A controller row: the object written and the object reconciled

A controller row has two objects. `krateo.audit.object_ref.*` (with
`k8s.namespace.name`) is the object the controller **wrote**, as the
apiserver's `objectRef` of that write names it. `krateo.audit.cause_ref.*` is
the object it **reconciled**: the custom resource whose reconcile made the
write. Write `cause_ref` on every row of a reconcile, also when the object
written is the reconciled resource itself (its status, its finalizers), so
that a reader joins on `cause_ref` alone. A write to an external endpoint
names the endpoint in `server.address` and the resource in `cause_ref`.
Only a controller writes `cause_ref`; for every other writer it does not
apply (`not-for-writer`). Once a row names a cause, its
`api_version`, `resource`, `name` and `uid` are required.

### The snowplow join

A person's write reaches a controller through the object it wrote. snowplow's
request row carries that object's `krateo.audit.object_ref.uid` and
`krateo.audit.object_ref.generation` as the apiserver returned them; the
row of a reconcile of that generation carries the same pair as
`krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid` and `krateo.audit.cause_ref.generation`.
The join reaches the request's `session.id` without touching the object:

```sql
SELECT h.LogAttributes['session.id']    AS session,
       c.ScopeName                      AS controller,
       c.LogAttributes['krateo.action'] AS action,
       c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.outcome'] AS outcome
FROM default.krateo_audit AS c
INNER JOIN default.krateo_audit AS h
   ON h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.uid'] = c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid']
  AND h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation'] = c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.generation']
WHERE h.ScopeName = 'github.com/krateo-platformops/snowplow/audit'
  AND c.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.cause_ref.uid'] != ''
  AND h.LogAttributes['krateo.audit.object_ref.generation'] != ''
```

A DELETE's request row carries no generation (the apiserver returns none for
a delete), so a reconcile a delete caused joins on `uid` alone. A
controller row written before v0.5.0 carries no `cause_ref`: it named the
object it reconciled in `object_ref`, so a join that spans those rows reads
`cause_ref` where it is set and `object_ref` otherwise.

## Kept deletions and pruned children

Two controller rows a helm-based controller writes for the children of the
resource it reconciles. Both name the child in `object_ref` and the
reconciled resource in `cause_ref`.

- **Kept deletion.** helm declined to delete a child, on an uninstall or an
  upgrade that no longer renders it, because it carries
  `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`. Verb `delete`, outcome `denied`,
  `krateo.audit.denial_reason` `kept_resource_policy`. No request was sent:
  no `http.request.method`, no status code. The reason is the key, not the
  LogRecord body: `Check` reads attributes only, and a reader filters on
  the key. The body adds nothing the record needs.
- **Pruned child.** helm deleted a child the new revision no longer renders.
  Verb `delete`, outcome `success`, no denial reason.

The `krateo.action` literal is the emit site's own. The literals below are
copied from `contract_records_test.go`, whose tests emit them through the
real Logs SDK and check the records (`audittest.AssertConformant`,
`AssertRequiredKeysDetected`, `AssertEnumsDetected`).

The emitter, built once. `logger` is the component's
`provider.Logger("<module>/audit")`: its scope name is the population the
live queries select, listed below under "Where each writer's records land".

```go
e := audit.New(logger,
	audit.WithWriter(audit.WriterController),
	audit.WithActor("system:serviceaccount:example-system:example-controller", audit.ClassController),
)
```

A kept deletion:

```go
ev := audit.Event{
	Action:       "helm.uninstall",
	Verb:         "delete",
	Outcome:      audit.OutcomeDenied,
	DenialReason: audit.DenialReasonKeptResourcePolicy,
	// No request was sent: no HTTPMethod, no StatusCode. No Message: the
	// reason is DenialReason, not the body.

	// object_ref: the child helm kept.
	Namespace:  "example-ns",
	Version:    "v1",
	Resource:   "persistentvolumeclaims",
	Kind:       "PersistentVolumeClaim",
	ObjectName: "example-data",
	Preview:    audit.PreviewFalse, // the Namespace's krateo.io/purpose label, read from the apiserver

	// cause_ref: the resource whose reconcile declined the delete.
	Cause: audit.CauseRef{
		Group:      "composition.krateo.io",
		Version:    "v1-2-0",
		Resource:   "exampleapps",
		Namespace:  "example-ns",
		Name:       "example-composition",
		UID:        "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000c1",
		Generation: 5,
	},
}
```

A pruned child:

```go
ev := audit.Event{
	Action:     "helm.upgrade",
	Verb:       "delete",
	HTTPMethod: "DELETE",
	Outcome:    audit.OutcomeSuccess,
	// StatusCode: the apiserver's answer, when the client returns it.

	// object_ref: the child helm deleted.
	Namespace:  "example-ns",
	Group:      "apps",
	Version:    "v1",
	Resource:   "deployments",
	Kind:       "Deployment",
	ObjectName: "example-worker",
	// ObjectUID: the child's uid, when the controller knows it.
	Preview: audit.PreviewFalse,

	// cause_ref: the resource whose reconcile pruned the child, at the
	// generation it reconciled.
	Cause: audit.CauseRef{
		Group:      "composition.krateo.io",
		Version:    "v1-2-0",
		Resource:   "exampleapps",
		Namespace:  "example-ns",
		Name:       "example-composition",
		UID:        "00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000c1",
		Generation: 4,
	},
}
```

## v0.3 keys (migration window W1)

Written side by side with their replacement by v0.4.x and v0.5.x, with the
same value, and removed by the release that closes W1, once the data shows no
row and no reader still needs them. Readers `coalesce` the two until the
last row without `krateo.audit.schema_version` expires. `Emit` adds the ones marked
"yes"; the others it writes only when the caller sets them.

| v0.3 key | replaced by | added by `Emit` |
|---|---|---|
| `outcome` | `krateo.audit.outcome` | yes |
| `enduser.id` | `user.name` | no: only where it is written today |
| `k8s.resource.group` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.api_group` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.version` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.api_version` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.resource` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.subresource` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.subresource` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.kind` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.kind` | yes |
| `k8s.resource.name` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.name` | yes |
| `k8s.object.uid` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.uid` | yes |
| `k8s.object.generation` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.generation` | yes |
| `k8s.object.resource_version` | `krateo.audit.object_ref.resource_version` | yes |

## Emit never drops a record

A record missing a key its writer must write is emitted without it, and
`krateo.audit.incomplete` names the missing key's marker (for a record with no
actor: `actor`). Each marker is counted under
`krateo.audit.records.incomplete{marker}`. `Check` reports such a key as
`incomplete`.

## Where each writer's records land

| instrumentation scope | writer | who |
|---|---|---|
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/snowplow/audit` | `request` | snowplow (H, and T for an agent going through /call) |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/authn/audit` | `request` | authn's login and /delegate records |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/authn/audit/controller` | `controller` | authn's background credential writes (certificate renewal, the step-up Secret sweep) |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/observability/gateway-audit` | `gateway` | the collector's gateway-audit projection |
| `github.com/krateo-platformops/audit` | `controller` | access-review and identity-lifecycle (split by ServiceName) |
| `rest-dynamic-controller/audit` | `controller` | rest-dynamic-controller |
| `request` | `gateway` | the agent gateway's pre-2026-10-22 access-log rows (pre-schema, the positive control) |
